Method of Attack: Using web archive file format (.MHT and .MHTML) to deploy backdoors
Attack chain starts with a RAR compression of a large web archive file containing a malicious Word document
Setting ZoneID property in file metadata to bypass Microsoft Office protection
Malicious VBA macro code execution after victim enables content in Word document
Payload dropped as guest.bmp, renamed to background.dll and executed via DLL export functions
Backdoor injected into rundll32.exe process running indefinitely in memory
Backdoor collects system information and sends encrypted data to C2 server hosted on Glitch
Scheduled task impersonating WinRAR update check to execute payload every 10 minutes
Impacted Systems: Microsoft Windows systems with Microsoft Office
Attack Vector: RAR compressed web archive file (.MHT/.MHTML) containing malicious Word document
Social engineering prompt to enable content in Word document
Use of ZoneID metadata to appear trustworthy
Use of Glitch cloud hosting service for C2 communication
Indicators of Compromise: Scheduled task mimicking WinRAR update check
C2 server URLs hosted on Glitch (now taken down)
Use of rundll32.exe process for backdoor injection
